summary: Distribute compiled Bun binaries for macOS and glibc Linux with checksum-verified installation, atomic self-update and a release workflow.
description: Add distribution to a Bun-compiled command-line tool: target builds, checksum files, a shell installer and an atomic update command. The release workflow checks and smoke-tests artifacts before publishing a tagged GitHub release. The default targets cover macOS and glibc Linux on Intel and ARM. Repository setup and publishing credentials remain maintainer actions; Windows builds are deferred and musl builds are optional.
seoDescription: Release Bun-compiled CLI binaries with target builds, checksums, a shell installer, atomic self-update and a tagged GitHub release workflow.

projectExamples.title: Installable diagnostics tool
projectExamples.description: Distribute a TypeScript diagnostics utility as downloadable executables with checksum verification. Implement the diagnostics commands in the base CLI.

projectExamples.title: Updatable terminal chat app
projectExamples.description: Combine this release fragment with openrouter-chat-cli to distribute the terminal application. Native TUI packages need target-specific build and smoke checks.

plain.whatItIs: Packages a command-line program built with Bun, a JavaScript runtime, into downloadable files for macOS and Linux, with an installer and an update command.
goodAt: Publishing downloads for Intel and ARM Macs and Linux computers
Checking each download against a checksum, a file fingerprint, before installing it
Updating an installed program in place, keeping the old copy if a download fails
notGoodAt: Windows computers; add that target separately.
Updating a copy run from source code; the update command only works for installed builds.

requests: let people install my Bun tool without installing its runtime
add an update command that preserves the working binary when a download fails
check release checksums before replacing an installed executable
build and smoke-test release binaries for both Intel and ARM machines
